title: OKR-driven feature gates & customer cohort mapping for Q2 Private/VPC
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: formalize a repeatable, OKR-aligned approach for gating features during Quarterly Private/VPC/on-prem rollout waves. This ticket defines (1) feature gate criteria mapped to product OKRs, (2) customer cohort segmentation for staged rollouts, and (3) the acceptance and rollback signals we will use to protect SLAs and quality during Q2 launches.

Context: multiple PM artifacts called out that customers need predictable upgrade windows and clear opt-in semantics for new Private features. Engineering requires concrete gating rules (latency, error budgets, owner on-call) before approving canary slices. This work sits between enterprise GTM and runtime teams to standardize decisions across initiatives.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Lina: Drafted initial cohort definitions (alpha/beta/controlled). Shared with ENG/CS for feedback.

2026-03-08 - PM review: Reworked OKR mapping so each gate ties to measurable SLOs (p95 latency, token-cost delta, and quality eval pass-rate).

Follow-ups: schedule 30m cross-functional sync weekly through rollout window; add an observability dashboard panel for cohort-level error budgets (Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/private-rollout-q2).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Feature gates documented and published in Confluence with clear pass/fail thresholds mapped to OKRs.
A2: Customer cohort definitions (Alpha/Beta/Controlled/GA) published and available to Sales/CS with onboarding checklist.
A3: Console UI flow for enabling/disabling gated features in Private installs implemented and QA’d (PR merged).
A4: Observability: cohort-level dashboard shows p50/p95 latency, error rate, and cost per token within burn-in window.
A5: Rollback runbook validated via a tabletop with Eng/Oncall/CS and documented incident playbook link.
A6: Security validation (KMS/HSM) step integrated and SEC sign-off recorded.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Preflight, Weeks -4 to -2): publish spec, finalize gating thresholds, and integrate security KMS checks.
Phase 1 (Alpha, Week -1 to Week 1): enable for 3 internal/beta customers (low QPS); monitor cost and p95 latency closely.
Phase 2 (Beta, Week 2 to Week 4): expand to 10 customers across two regions; run A/B quality evals on production prompts.
Phase 3 (Controlled GA, Week 5 to Week 8): allow opt-in for larger customers with reserved capacity; begin deprecation of legacy flags.
GA: feature flips on by default for new accounts; older customers migrated with 30d notice and assisted rollout.
Rollback criteria: sustained p95 latency > 2x baseline for 30m, error rate > 1% absolute delta, or quality eval drop > 5% on key prompt set.
decisions: Decision 2026-03-04: Use cohort sizes (3 internal -> 10 beta -> controlled GA) rather than percent-based rollouts to simplify billing reconciliation.
Decision 2026-03-06: Accept runtime compatibility requirement — quantized 8-bit model variants must be tested in Alpha before Beta expansion.
Decision 2026-03-08: Tie one OKR (Reduce Private p95 latency by 10%) to gate progression; product managers may withhold rollout if metric not met.
blockers: ENG-22431: Runtime kernel compatibility matrix outstanding — blocks Alpha signoff.
SEC-9087: KMS validation automation needed for onprem installs to enter Beta.
DOCS-1122: Customer-facing rollout docs not yet reviewed by Solutions Engineering.
